WITH race_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    r.raceId,
    c.country,
    COUNT(*) as entry_count,
    SUM(cr.points) as total_points
  FROM constructorResults cr
  JOIN races r ON cr.raceId = r.raceId
  JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
  GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country
),
avg_entries AS (
  SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_count
  FROM race_stats
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT rs.*, ae.avg_count
  FROM race_stats rs, avg_entries ae
  WHERE rs.entry_count > ae.avg_count
),
ranked_above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    *,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY entry_count DESC) as dr
  FROM above_average
)
SELECT 
  raa.raceId,
  raa.country,
  raa.total_points,
  raa.entry_count,
  (raa.entry_count - raa.avg_count) as difference_from_average
FROM ranked_above_avg raa
WHERE raa.dr <= 10
ORDER BY difference_from_average DESC

assumptions.assumption: If fewer than 10 distinct entry counts exist among races above average, no races are selected (empty result). The request does not specify this edge case.

alternatives.interpretation: Use ROW_NUMBER to rank races by position rather than distinct value. With ROW_NUMBER, the '10th-highest' is the entry count at the 10th row position when sorted by count descending (treating tied races as separate rows), which may differ from the 10th distinct value when there are multiple races tied at certain counts.
alternatives.sql:
WITH race_stats AS (
  SELECT r.raceId, c.country, COUNT(*) as entry_count, SUM(cr.points) as total_points
  FROM constructorResults cr
  JOIN races r ON cr.raceId = r.raceId
  JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
  GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country
),
avg_entries AS (SELECT AVG(entry_count) as avg_count FROM race_stats),
above_average AS (SELECT rs.*, ae.avg_count FROM race_stats rs, avg_entries ae WHERE rs.entry_count > ae.avg_count),
ranked_above_avg AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY entry_count DESC) as rn FROM above_average),
cutoff_value AS (SELECT entry_count FROM ranked_above_avg WHERE rn = 10)
SELECT raa.raceId, raa.country, raa.total_points, raa.entry_count, (raa.entry_count - raa.avg_count) as difference_from_average
FROM above_average raa
WHERE raa.entry_count >= (SELECT entry_count FROM cutoff_value)
ORDER BY difference_from_average DESC
